content: 1. Lorazepate affects the metabolism of hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. It is recommended to avoid or use an alternative drug and monitor closely. 2. Clotrimazole decreases the level or effect of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 3. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of clozapine by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and an alternative drug should be used. 4. Clozapine and lopinavir both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug as this combination is contraindicated. 5. Cobicistat increases the level or effect of ritonavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This interaction is serious, and an alternative drug should be used. 6. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of cobicistat by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 7. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of cobimetinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 8. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of cobimetinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 9. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of topical cocaine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 10. Lopinavir decreases the effects of codeine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 11. Ritonavir decreases the level or effect of codeine by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2D6 metabolism, preventing its conversion to the active metabolite morphine. This interaction is serious, and an alternative drug should be used. 12. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of colchicine by mechanisms involving P-glycoprotein and CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. Colchicine is contraindicated in patients with renal or hepatic impairment when used with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors. 13. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of conivaptan by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 14. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of conivaptan by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. This combination is contraindicated. 15. Conivaptan increases the level or effect of ritonavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 16. Conivaptan increases the level or effect of lopinavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 17. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 18. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 19. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of vaginal conjugated estrogens by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. 20. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of copanlisib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 21. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of copanlisib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. If concomitant use with strong CYP3A inhibitors cannot be avoided, reduce the copanlisib dose to 45 mg. 22. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of cortisone by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism and P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Monitor closely. 23. Cortisone decreases the level or effect of ritonavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 24. Crizotinib increases the levels of ritonavir by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Ritonavir increases the levels of crizotinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 25. Lopinavir increases the levels of crizotinib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 26. Crizotinib and lopinavir both increase the QTc interval. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 27. Crofelemer increases the levels of lopinavir and ritonavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Use caution and monitor closely. 28. Ritonavir increases the level or effect of cyclophosphamide by affecting hepatic enzyme CYP2B6 and CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 29. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of cyclophosphamide by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Monitor closely. 30. Lopinavir increases the level or effect of dabigatran by inhibiting the P-glycoprotein (MDR1) efflux transporter. Use caution and monitor closely. Avoid coadministration if CrCl <30 mL/min for atrial fibrillation or <50 mL/min for DVT/PE treatment. 34. Ritonavir increases the levels of dabrafenib by decreasing its metabolism via hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 37. Lopinavir increases the levels of dabrafenib by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 38. Dasatinib increases the level or effect of ritonavir and lopinavir by affecting hepatic and intestinal enzyme CYP3A4 metabolism. Avoid or use an alternative drug. 47.
